title: PAL says its jet fuel supply 'sufficient for foreseeable future'
content: MANILA -- Philippine Airlines (PAL) said Wednesday it had secured enough jet fuel supply to support its operations "for the foreseeable future." In a statement, PAL said it was working with fuel suppliers, industry partners, and the government to ensure that operations are stable and efficient in the long term. "Philippine Airlines is closely monitoring global and regional developments affecting jet fuel supply and pricing...the airline recognizes that global supply conditions remain dynamic," the flag carrier said. Last week, the Civil Aeronautics Board raised the fuel surcharge level from Level 4 to Level 8 from April 1 to 15. This means surcharges of between P253 and P787 for domestic passengers, and between P835 and P6,209 for international passengers. On Monday, budget carrier Cebu Pacific said it was suspending some of its routes as global fuel prices continued to soar. The Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines (CAAP) has since lowered airport landing and terminal fees. Aeronautical fees for both landing and takeoff will be cut by nearly 50 percent starting April. The passenger service charge for international travel will also be reduced to P700 from P900. Passenger service charge for domestic travel at international airports will be lowered from P350 to between P150 to P200.

title: Philippines eyeing Russian oil– Marcos
content: MANILA — The Philippines is working to secure fuel supply from Russia, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said on Tuesday, hours before he declared a state of national energy emergency due to an “imminent danger” on the “availability and stability of energy supply.” The President government is “still working on that” deal, Marcos told Bloomberg in an interview in Malacañang. “Russia is not a traditional supplier of crude oil to the Philippines or any energy supply, but we are exploring that as well,” he said. “Basically, we are trying anything, everything to secure supply because that’s the one thing that we can do about,” he said. “The pricing is going to be a much more difficult challenge because everyone is a price taker when it comes to oil,” he added. The United States — the Philippines’ traditional ally — earlier imposed sanctions against Russian oil and trade, but earlier this month, US President Donald Trump eased those restrictions as Iran continues to block the Strait of Hormuz, where 20 percent of the world’s oil supply passes through. Nearly a month since US-Israeli forces launched air strikes against Iran, the Philippines is “doing better than a month in terms of fuel supply — maybe 45 days more or less, depends on diesel or gasoline,” Marcos said. The country, which imports nearly 100 percent of its oil, has also been sourcing fertilizer from Indonesia and China, refined fuel from Japan and South Korea, and oil from Malaysia, he said. On March 24, Marcos signed an executive order declaring a state of national energy emergency, which authorizes certain government agencies to come up with various policies to address oil supply woes, without being impeded by laws on procurement and pricing, among others. Marcos earlier certified as urgent a measure that would allow the executive to either suspend or reduce the fuel excise tax, but he has yet to sign the bill, a week after Congress passed it on final reading.

title: Gov’t secures 22.5 million liters of diesel amid state of energy emergency
content: MANILA — The Department of Energy (DOE) has brought in the country’s first shipment of imported diesel under the Emergency Energy Security Program, delivering about 22.5 million liters or 142,000 barrels to reinforce the national fuel supply as the Philippines confronts a state of energy emergency. The DOE said the shipment is part of the Marcos administration’s directive to stabilize reserves and shield transport, industry, and other vital sectors from the impact of global oil market volatility. Implemented in coordination with the Philippine National Oil Company (PNOC) and PNOC Exploration Corporation (PNOC EC), the program aims to secure up to two million barrels of additional oil for the country. Energy Secretary Sharon S. Garin underscored the urgency of the measure: “Patuloy ang pagtutok ng DOE upang madagdagan ang suplay ng langis sa bansa. Ang mabilis na pagdating ng diesel na ito ay bahagi ng mga hakbang para hindi maantala ang biyahe, hanapbuhay, at pang-araw-araw na buhay ng bawat Pilipino.” The DOE emphasized that the initiative is aligned with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s Executive Order No. 110, which directs agencies to safeguard the nation’s energy needs during periods of global uncertainty.

title: LPG prices also set to rise
content: MANILA - After the series of bigtime price increases in diesel, gasoline, and kerosene, now comes LPG. Regasco President Arnel Ty has sounded off a hefty price increase next week as shipping costs multiplied by 4 to 5 times due to the war in the Middle East. According to Ty, the increase in shipping costs alone is already equivalent to a hike of P30/kilo. On top of that, the contract price of LPG is now higher by $95/metric ton, which translates to an increase of around P5/kilo. If sustained until the last day of March, it means the increase will range from P35-P40/kilo for April 1, which is a whopping P385-P440 spike on an 11-kilogram cylinder.  SUPPLY ENOUGH FOR 30 DAYS Ty said the industry has asked the Department of Energy for help in procuring supply from other countries through a government-to-government arrangement. According to Ty, consumers need not panic as supply remains sufficient to cover demand for 30-35 days. But the industry is asking the DOE to get in touch with US, Russia, Japan, South Korea, Australia, and Canada for possible supply contracts.  BRACE FOR HIGHER POWER RATES Meanwhile, Energy Secretary Sharon Garin has also alerted consumers that the government is doing everything to avoid the estimated P4/kilowatt hour increase in Meralco rates for April. Garin said this is due to higher cost of contracted power, as well as more expensive power from the spot market.  The energy regulatory commission has ordered the suspension of the Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao spot markets in order to avoid the higher prices and maintain administered prices on electricity traded in the market. But Energy Regulatory Commission Chairman Nino Juan said aside from the market suspension, the commission will also issue an order for all private distribution utilities and electric coops to stagger any rate adjustment deem too high for the consumers. Juan said all DUs and electric coops are directed to submit first to the ERC all automatic overall rate adjustments for the next months before it is announced or implemented.  UPDATE ON WORLD OIL PRICES After 3 trading days, gasoline and kerosene prices are finally in negative territory for the first time since the war started. But diesel is still higher: Diesel       P7.00/L ⬆️ Gasoline   P0.10/L ⬇️ Kerosene  P1.20/L ⬇️ But these figures still do not include the risk premium costs added by suppliers due to the war in the Middle East.

title: DSWD points to companies for missing drivers in payout lists: 'Baka lumagpas sila sa quota'
content: Delivery riders receive cash relief assistance at the Makati City Hal quadrangle on Friday morning. Eon Sanchez, ABS-CBN News MANILA — Delivery service riders lined up at the Makati City Hall quadrangle before daybreak on Friday as the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) opened its latest round of cash assistance payouts, distributing P5,000 each to beneficiaries scheduled for March 27, 2026. By 6:30 a.m., riders were already queued for verification, hoping to claim their aid before starting their shifts. Free pandesal were also given out after the recipients completed the process. The DSWD expects 1,600 delivery riders to claim assistance on Friday, including those who failed to show up during Thursday’s rollout. The agency’s week-long schedule allocated specific days per transport subgroup: Tuesday for TNVS drivers, Wednesday for jeepney and PUJ operators, Thursday and Friday for delivery riders, and Saturday for motorcycle taxi drivers. DSWD Secretary Rex Gatchalian said the agency has been receiving fewer complaints about missing names — a problem that has repeatedly surfaced in previous aid distributions. But he stressed that gaps in the masterlists trace back to the companies that submitted them. “I would like to say na mas konti yung mga nakukuha naming complaints na wala sa listahan because working with DICT, nakikita namin yung list na sinubmit ng mga companies operating it,” Gatchalian said. He explained that the DSWD merely implements the distribution based on the data provided to them. “Challenge here is kami yung humaharap sa tao pagka wala sa listahan pero hindi namin minsan mapaliwanag bakit wala sila sa listahan dahil hindi naman kami gumawa ng listahan,” he said. Gatchalian pointed to “tempo drivers” — temporary drivers onboarded by platforms but not registered with the LTFRB — as a major contributor to the inconsistencies. “Napakalaking porsyento ng kanilang mga driver, wala. Kasi nga yun yung natalakay ko couple of days ago. They have this type of drivers na in-onboard nila, called tempo drivers. Mga temporary drivers ito so they’re not registered with LTFRB officially pero nag-o-operate sila dahil in-onboard sila,” he said. He added that some companies may be hesitant to provide complete lists because doing so would reveal how far they have exceeded their allowed quotas. “Talagang sinabi na namin: ibigay nila sa amin nang buo yung listahan. Wag nilang i-filter. I think, they’re scared kasi of admitting na nag-onboard sila nang walang mga CPC o yung mga permits and lumagpas na sila dun sa quota na allowed for ride-hailing,” he said. Gatchalian also assured transport workers that the assistance will not end with this week’s payouts. “Wag silang mag-alala. Sabi naman sa utos ng ating pangulo, hindi naman to isang beses lang. Sigurado kami na magkakaroon ng mga susunod na mga payout dahil naiintindihan namin na patuloy na tumataas ang presyo ng petrolyo,” he said. “Ang sabi ng pangulo, for as long as it takes. So nakahanda na yung pondo ng DSWD,” he added, noting that P30 billion has been earmarked for transport sector support until June, with another P30 billion allotted for the second half of the year. For riders at the payout site, the cash aid offers short-term relief amid rising costs and shrinking incomes. Three-year delivery rider Eriberto Mendiola said the P5,000 will go to family expenses and their small store. “[Pang-gastos] sa pamilya ko tapos pandagdag na rin po sa pampuhunan sa negosyo/tindahan namin,” he said. But with prices and fuel costs climbing, Mendiola admitted the assistance feels limited. “Parang kulang pa rin kasi sobrang taas na rin ng mga bilihin e. Sumasabay pa yung gasolina.” “Ideal siguro mga kahit mga doble. Kahit 10k, okay na,” he added. Five-year rider Christopher Natividad said he plans to buy a new passenger helmet and pay debts. “Pambili ng helmet saka yung iba, pambayad ng utang,” he said. “Malaking bagay po kasi mahal na yung gasolina ngayon.” Asked if the aid is enough, he said: “Sakto lang. Malaking bagay din,” adding that he is grateful regardless of the amount: “Okay na yun kung magkano lang ibigay. May trabaho naman eh.”

title: Robinsons Retail to exit Philippine Stock Exchange
content:
Robinsons Retail Holdings Inc. (RRHI) is planning to exit the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE). File photo MANILA — Robinsons Retail Holdings Inc. (RRHI) is planning to exit the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE). In a filing, Robinsons Retail told the PSE that JE Holdings, Inc.--a privately-held investment company of the Gokongwei family--wants to make a tender offer to
voluntarily delist RRHI from the PSE. The tender offer is at P48.30 per share. Trading of RRHI stocks was suspended at 9:35 a.m. on Friday to give investors time to assess the delisting. Trading will resume on March 30 at 9 a.m. No Brand stores in PH to close by end of June Two companies have delisted from the PSE in the last 3 years-- Metro Pacific Investment Corporation and 8990 Holdings . In March 2025, the PSE cut the minimum public float requirement for IPOs from 20 percent to 15 percent, in the hopes that more companies will go public. Officials considered 2024 a tepid listing year, with only 3 new companies--OceanaGold Philippines, NexGen Energy, and Citicore Renewable Energy-- being listed on the PSE. But in 2025, only two companies debuted on the Philippine Stock Exchange: Maynilad and Cebu-based Top Line Business Development Corporation. Resort developer Hann Holdings has yet to debut on the state bourse despite getting SEC clearance in July 2025. Meanwhile, GCash is still eyeing an initial public offering but has no timeline yet.

title: Palace refutes possible ‘energy lockdown’ in PH despite oil supply woes
content: Employees fill tanks at a gas station in Quezon City on June 28, 2019. George Calvelo, ABS-CBN News/File MANILA — Malacañang on Friday dismissed worries over a possible "energy lockdown" as tightening oil supply force pump prices to continuously hike nearly a month since the Middle East war broke out. “Sa ngayon po, as we speak, wala po tayong nakikita,” Communications Undersecretary Claire Castro told Palace reporters. The Department of Energy (DOE) has issued guidelines to allow the use of cheaper fuel and more coal to generate electricity, she said. “The ERC (Energy Regulatory Commission) has now suspended the electricity market so we can have more coal, renewable energy and even Malampaya-assisted power… All that and more para posibleng maibaba ang presyo,” she said. “Maganda din po na ang mga solar companies ay maka-comply sa kanilang mga obligasyon,” she added. The Philippine government is also coordinating with other countries to ensure that there will be sufficient supply while tensions in the Gulf region remain high, the Palace official said. “Ayaw po nating mapunta sa worst case scenario. Naghahanap po talaga tayo ng sources para yung supply ng petrolyo ay hindi mahinto at magtuloy tuloy din po para sa ating mga kababayan,” Castro said. “Ang sabi din po niya (Marcos Jr.), there is nothing to be panicked about,” she said. “Ang pagsasagawa ng Executive Order 110 ay para hindi tayo makarating sa tinatawag na krisis. Ang lahat ng maaring ibigay na tulong, proyekto para maibsan ang impact na krisis ay gagawin,” she said. Earlier this week, Marcos Jr. declared a state of national energy emergency to allow government to have more leeway in the procurement of additional oil supply, and signed a bill allowing the executive branch to suspend or reduce excise tax on petroleum products. Despite these measures, pump prices continue to hover around P100 per liter leaving consumers calling for more interventions from the government. Malacañang maintained that it is still in the process of studying the implementation of a price freeze, noting that the government needs to balance the interests of all sectors.

title: Peso hits new historic low of P60.55 vs dollar
content: MANILA — The Philippine peso continued to fall anew, touching a fresh record low of P60.55 to the dollar. This was lower than the P60.30 to the US dollar at the close of trading on March 23. In a Thursday press briefing, Bangko Sentral Governor Eli Remolona said the central bank is looking at all data and information as they remain vigilant to keep prices stable amid the war in the Middle East. He also assured the public that the weakening of the peso is not necessarily a bad thing.  “So far it hasn’t merited heavy intervention... The peso, where it’s going, seems to help with our current account deficit, seems to help with our exports. It’s not necessarily a bad thing,” he added. The next scheduled Monetary Policy meeting will be on April 23, 2026. Remolona said with the ongoing conlfict abroad, they may hold more off-cycle meetings.

title: Motorist assistance program to roll out in expressways during Holy Week
content: MANILA — The Metro Pacific Tollways Cor. (MPTC) and its network of expressways announced it is rolling out a motorist assistance program from March 27 to April 6, in preparation for the expected surge of commuters during the Holy Week break. The motorist assistance program includes: Roadworks, lane closures, and maintenance activities will be suspended during this period. Traffic teams are also on standby to activate counterflow schemes when conditions permit. MPTC reminded the public planning to traverse NLEX to anticipate heavy northbound traffic from Wednesday afternoon to Thursday afternoon. Increased southbound volume may also be expected during the afternoon and evening hours on Saturday and Sunday. Motorists are also advised to expect heavy southbound traffic on early Monday morning. MPTC also reminded motorists to ensure sufficient balance in their RFID accounts, inspect their vehicles before traveling, stay well-rested, and follow speed limits and traffic regulations. Updates are available via the official social media pages as well as the MPT DriveHub app, to keep motorists informed on the latest situation on the MPTC expressways, it said. NLEX Corp. on Friday said it is already seeing a 3-percent increase in traffic volume ahead of the Holy Week on top of the normal daily average of 360,000 vehicles. Expressway concessionaires previously announced a two-month toll discount for PUV, PUB and freight services starting March 23 to cushion the impact of the surging oil prices. Meanwhile, the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority assured the public it is implementing a 'no-absent, no day-of'f policy among its frontline personnel, especially traffic enforcers and deputies who will assist motorists during the Holy Week break. The agency reminded the public to immediately contact MMDA's Hotline 136 for assistance. MANILA — Prices of fish and vegetables at the Pasig City Mega Market remain mostly stable as Holy Week approaches, though vendors and consumers anticipate potential increases in the coming days due to higher demand. Fish vendor Owen Tentengco said supplies are still adequate, helping keep prices manageable for now. “Medyo bumaba ngayon nang konti. Ewan lang natin sa Holy Week kung baka medyo tumaas. Depende sa dating ng kalakal yun,” he said. He added that sellers avoid raising prices unnecessarily. “Ang hirap din magbenta pag mahal. Kaya hindi kami nagtataas,” he added, noting that any adjustment may begin midweek. “Siguro Miyerkules Santo, tataasan. Pero Lunes Santo hanggang Martes Santo, wala pa.” Shoppers also expect movement in prices. Roberto Ramos, who plans to prepare fish and vegetables for Holy Week, said that while prices remain manageable, increases are possible. “Sa ngayon, di pa gaano ramdam pero baka sa susunod na araw, tataas na rin lahat ng mga bilihin dito,” he said. Vegetable vendor Maybelle confirmed that only carrots have shown early movement. “Ngayong paparating na Holy Week, baka tumaas pa yung presyo ng gulay. Di ba bawal sa karne ngayon,” she said. “Yung mga kinukuhanan din, tumataas yung presyo tas tumataas rin kami,” she added. “Pag tumataas yung gasolina, tumataas rin yung presyo.” For households with tight budgets, the anticipated increases pose a challenge. Neng Alcantara, who allocates P6,000 for a week’s supply of food for a 10-member household, said price hikes strain their budget. “Pag tumataas yung bilihin… parang masakit sa dibdib yun. Katulad naming mahihirap, hindi kaya ang budget na malaki. Kailangan maliit lang. Magkano lang naman ang kinikita namin sa isang buwan. Magpalagay na 10,000, kakasya ba yun?” she added. Widow of Baguio-based photog: 'Heaven is my husband and daughter'
content: The widow of a Baguio-based photographer who died during a charity mission in Itogon, Benguet on Friday tells how she will miss her husband, whom she described as her “heaven". Ma. Joanne Hendrix Ongchangco told ABS-CBN News her last moments with husband Neil Clark Ongchangco, who died Friday afternoon. “Yung the day before kasi nung outreach is graduation ng anak namin sa kinder, so parang we spent the day umattend nung graduation tapos nagpunta kami sa (Camp) John Hay after. Tapos yun, kinagabihan..natulog kami ng maaga kasi maaga din siyang aalis,” Ongchangco said. According to Ongchangco, it has been common for her husband to join missions to give back to the community. Neil is a member of Baguio Photographers Club who regularly conducts a free photo session to graduating students in their community. “Tradition kasi yun ng Baguio Photographers Club na kapag may mga graduating na students, parang regalo ng club na bibigyan nila ng graduation portrait,” Ongchangco. She vividly recalled that on the early morning of Friday, her husband woke up early for the scheduled mission. Ongchangco said her husband was able to attend the kindergarten graduation of their 6-year old daughter Camille. “Maaga siyang umalis…the day before kasi nung  outreach is graduation ng anak namin sa kinder, so we spend the day na umattend nung graduation - nag-bonding kami sa (Camp) John Hay after, tapos parang kinagabihan, natulog kami ng maaga kasi maaga siyang aalis,” Ongchangco recalled. She is now trying to explain their situation to her daughter, but admitted she doesn’t know how. “Ang alam lang niya, wala na yung papa niya - pero yung concept ng death na kung ano yung consequences, kung ano yung mangyayari after, wala siyang idea - basta ang alam lang niya, wala na yung papa niya,” Ongchangco told ABS-CBN News. Ongchangco shared that she and her husband never had heated arguments, describing him as gentle and loving. “Very gentle, kasi malambin…hindi kami yung nag-aaway na nagsasagutan, walang ganon. Kapag naramdaman na namin yung tension, tumatahimik na kami - hintayin naming kumalma kami tsaka kami mag-uusap,” said Ongchangco. Ongchangco described her relationship with her husband and their daughter as “heaven.” “Kasi yung concept ko ng heaven is yung nasa-sandwich ako nung anak ko tapos yung husband ko. Yung magkakatabi kaming matulog, yun na yung simpleng kaligayahan ko sa araw-araw. At the end of the day, katabi ko siyang matulog, katabi ko yung anak kong matulog…tas hindi ko alam kung paano kasi wala na siya,” Ongchangco said.

title: On father's birthday, VP Sara thanks Duterte supporters for their loyalty
content: MANILA (UPDATED) — Vice President Sara Duterte on Saturday  thanked her father former President Rodrigo Duterte's followers and supporters for their loyalty as she stressed on his birthday that his detention by the International Criminal Court is a matter of national sovereignty. In a message, Duterte thanked "groups, volunteers, and the millions of Filipinos here and abroad" who she said organized celebrations for her father's birthday. "Your loyalty to him is a testament to a leadership that truly prioritized the safety and dignity of every Filipino family," she said. "But as we celebrate, we also stand firm. The defense of his rights is a defense of our national sovereignty." The Dutertes and their supporters have taken the position that the former president was kidnapped when the Philippine National Police arrested him in March 2025 and transported him to The Hague in the Netherlands. The government has said it was fulfilling a commitment to assist the Interpol in serving arrest warrants. The ICC's Pre-Trial Chamber I held confirmation of charges proceedings last month on crimes against humanity allegations against the elder Duterte related to his bloody but popular "war on drugs" while he was president. "We must remain vigilant against the weaponization of the law and the unconstitutional intrusion of foreign bodies that seek to bypass our own courts," Vice President Duterte said. "Our justice system must remain independent, serving only the mandate of the Filipino people and never the interests of foreign powers." Vice President Duterte also joined the Parada Dabawenyo civic parade on Saturday to culminate the 89th Araw ng Davao, the city’s founding anniversary celebration. Traditionally held in mid-March, this year’s parade took place on March 28 to coincide with the former president's 81st birthday. More than 400 contingents from local government units, educational institutions, organizations, and other sectors participated in the parade, which did away with floats and vehicles because of the fuel crisis. Various groups and organizations supporting the Dutertes also joined the parade and called for his release. Vice President Duterte and her political allies arrived at San Pedro Square to deliver speeches. Among those in her entourage were former Marcos supporter Vic Rodriguez; Cavite 4th District Rep. Francisco “Kiko” Barzaga;  Reina Mercedes, Isabela Vice Mayor Harold Respicio; Batangas 1st District Rep. Leandro Leviste and former Comelec Commissioner Rowena Guanzon. — with Hernel Tocmo MANILA — Motorcycle taxi and delivery riders received assistance from the Department of Social Welfare and Development and the Land Transportation Franchise and Regulatory Board on Saturday, as government distribution of aid continued for a second week. As of 12 noon, around 4,250 riders had already received their P5,000 subsidy at the Quezon Memorial Circle. One of them was 29-year-old Noel Ebora, who went straight to a gasoline station to fill up his tank before beginning his shift as an MC taxi rider. "Malaking tulong po ito para sa mga rider po katulad po namin mga nagtatrabaho kasi po bihira lang naman po ito… magpagas po ano nito para mamaya daretso biyahe ma po," Ebora said. With only two bars of fuel left beforehand, he spent P300 to get a full tank. The remaining P3,700 will go to his wife and three children to help cover household expenses for the Holy Week, especially with the kids currently on school vacation. "Kay misis po pangbayad po ng kuryente, mga bill… Hanggang tatlong araw lang po siguro… Matumal ang biyahe sa Holy Week. After Holy week, wala na, back to biyahe na ulit," Ebora added. Meanwhile, not everyone who lined up was able to receive their subsidy. Mark Manzano, 32, arrived at the Circle as early as 6 a.m., but after four hours of waiting in line, he was informed that he was not included in the list of beneficiaries. He had planned to use the subsidy for household expenses and for his five-month-old baby. "Nakakadismaya syempre, ang haba-haba ng pila namin, alas-6 pa kami dito eh... Sana hindi sila namimili, dapat lahat ng rider nabibigyan. Kahit kasi bawat platform tanggap sila ng tanggap tapos pagdating ng mga tao eh, pagdating ng ganitong sitwasyon wala siła," Manzano complained. DSWD Secretary Rex Gatchalian said a special payout will be arranged for drivers who were not included in the list. "Alam natin na, like here, ang listahan galing sa mga TNC (transport network company) nila, may mga ilan-ilan pa rin na hindi nasama ng mga kumpanya nila, ng mga platform nila. So we will talk to their platforms to give us the (complete) list," he explained. A rider volunteer from a ride-hailing company assisting those not on the list said some names may have been excluded due to a system error. "Baka kasi nagkaroon ng mga lapses, nagkaroon ng error sa system kasi meron mga nagsasabi yung mga bago[ng rider sa kumpanya] na isama tapos yung matatagal ang wala sa listahan," explained Jethroy De Mesa, a rider volunteer assistant of JoyRide Superapp. "Pinapai-scan na QR code para po ito sa mga wala yung sa listahan. Bali magkakaroon ng panibagong data para maisama sila sa susunod na payout… special payout kung tawagin" he added. Meanwhile, a viral social media post of a jeepney driver asking passengers for extra tips has raised questions about how short-lived these subsidies are. Gatchalian said he had seen the post and reassured the public that the cash assistance program will continue as long as fuel prices keep rising amid the conflict in the Middle East. "Sasabayan natin itong patuloy na pagtaas ng presyo ng petrolyo. Pauna lang po, may second and I hope may third pa. Ang assurance namin sa inyo, walang tsuper na maiiwanan at sisiguraduhin namin na sa oras ng kagipitan kasama niyo kami," Gatchalian added. Fuel prices are expected to continue to increase further in the coming weeks, along with LPG and electricity rates. MANILA — Acting Justice Secretary Fredderick Vida is eyeing a ‘zero backlog’ on the Good Conduct Time Allowance (GCTA) applications of persons deprived of liberty (PDLs). He said digitalization efforts have been helpful in expediting the processing of applications for the policy, which incentivizes good behavior by giving PDLs a chance at earlier release. “I think we're on the right trajectory. ‘Yung projection natin na very soon, very soon, we will have zero backlog na in processing of all the GCTA applications,” he told ABS-CBN News in an exclusive interview after he led a ceremonial activity for the release of 1,239 persons deprived of liberty (PDLs) from February 14 to March 28, 2026 at the New Bilibid Prison in Muntinlupa City Saturday, March 28. Vida said around 31,000 GCTA applications have been approved under the Marcos Jr. administration, which he said is more than the past three administrations have granted. "Less than 2,000" are still under review, according to Vida. The acting DOJ chief said he will provide a more comprehensive report on his press briefing next week as he marks his 100th day in the post. Meanwhile, the Bureau of Corrections said the zero backlog goal “signals stronger support for prisoners’ rights and rehabilitation.” It also said, quoting Director General Gregorio Catapang Jr., that releasing PDLs “alleviates overcrowding in detention facilities but also gives former inmates a chance to rebuild their lives and contribute positively to society.” In his speech, Vida encouraged the newly released PDLs to "recover" their lives "one step at a time". title: Yemen's Houthis confirm launching attack on Israel
content: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis confirmed on Saturday (March 28) that they have launched missiles at Israel, their first such attack since the Iran war began, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the U.S. expected to conclude military operations within weeks.The Houthis, whose involvement risks broadening and prolonging a war that has entered its fifth week, said their operations would continue until the "aggression" on all fronts ended.Israel said it had intercepted a missile from Yemen.The Houthis had said on Friday (March 27) they were prepared to act if what the group called an escalation against Iran and the "Axis of Resistance" continued in the war.The group has shown an ability to strike targets far beyond Yemen and disrupt shipping lanes around the Arabian Peninsula and the Red Sea, as they did in support of Hamas in Gaza after October 7, 2023.The war, launched with U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28, has spread across the Middle East, killing thousands and causing the biggest disruption ever to energy supplies, hitting the global economy and fuelling inflation fears.(Production: Khaled Abdullah, Abdulrhman Al-Ansi, Lisa Giles-Keddie) Northeastern Tehran experienced heavy bombardment in the early hours of Saturday as the Iranian capital came under one the most intense aerial strikes from the United States and Israel over the recent days.Explosions flashed and dense smoke billowed over the skyline of the capital, while the intermittent roar of air defense interceptors echoed across multiple districts, according to a China Media Group (CMG) reporter on the ground.Based on the reporter’s observation, the latest round of airstrikes may be the most significant one by United States and Israel against Iran recently.Meanwhile, a heavy water research reactor facility in central Iran’s Khondab was attacked by U.S.-Israeli airstrikes on Friday, Iran’s semi-official Fars news agency reported.No casualties or danger to residents in the area have been reported so far, Fars added, citing local authorities.The Atomic Energy Organisation of Iran later confirmed the attack.Furthermore, a yellowcake production plant in central Iran’s Yazd province was also hit by U.S.-Israeli strikes, with no radioactive leaks reported so far, semi-official Mehr news agency reported.The plant, inaugurated in May 2023, produces yellowcake, a uranium concentrate powder obtained from leach solutions and serving as an intermediate step in the processing of uranium ores.The Israel Defense Forces confirmed the two attacks in two statements. MINNEAPOLIS — Massive nationwide protests against US President Donald Trump are expected Saturday as millions of people vent fury over what they see as his authoritarian bent and other forms of cruel, law-trampling governance. It is the third time in less than a year that Americans will take to the streets as part of a grassroots movement called "No Kings," the most vocal and visual conduit for opposition to Trump since he began his second term in January 2025. And now they have something new to fume over -- the war in Iran that Trump launched alongside Israel, with ever-shifting goals and timelines for completion. The first such nationwide protest day came in June on Trump's 79th birthday and coincided with a military parade in Washington that he insisted on holding. Several million people turned out, from New York to San Francisco and many places in between. The second "No Kings" day in October drew an estimated seven million protesters, according to organizers. The goal now is to bring out even more people on Saturday, as Trump's approval rating is low at around 40 percent and midterm elections loom in November, when Trump's Republicans could lose control of both chambers. Just as Trump is worshipped by many in his "Make America Great Again" movement, on the other side of America's wide political chasm he is disliked or even loathed with equal passion. Trump foes bemoan his penchant for ruling by executive decree, his use of the Justice Department to prosecute opponents, his embrace of fossil fuels and climate change denial even as the planet warms, his fight against racial and gender diversity programs, and his newfound taste for flexing US military power after campaigning as a man of peace. "Since the last time we marched, this administration has dragged us deeper into war," said Naveed Shah of Common Defense, a veterans association that belongs to the "No Kings" movement. "At home, we've watched citizens killed in the streets by militarized forces. We've seen families torn apart and immigrant communities targeted. All of it done in the name of one man trying to rule like a king," Shah said. Organizers say more than 3,000 rallies are planned, an increase from the last protest day, in major cities coast to coast and in suburbs and rural areas — even in the Alaskan town of Kotzebue, above the Arctic circle. Minnesota will be a key focal point, returning to the limelight months after becoming ground zero for the national debate over Trump's violent immigration crackdown. Legendary rocker Bruce Springsteen, a fierce critic of the president, is scheduled to perform in St. Paul, the capital of the northern state, his song "Streets of Minneapolis." It is a ballad he wrote and recorded in the space of 24 hours in memory of Renee Good and Alex Pretti, Americans shot and killed by federal agents during protests in frigid January weather against Trump's immigration offensive. "Masked secret police terrorizing our communities. An illegal, catastrophic war putting us in danger and driving up our costs. Attacks on our freedom of speech, our civil rights, our freedom to vote. Costs pushing families to the brink. Trump wants to rule over us as a tyrant," the "No Kings" movement said. It said what began in 2025 as a simple day of defiance has mushroomed into a powerful movement of national resistance to the Trump administration. Organizers say two-thirds of those who plan to rally Saturday do not live in big cities, which in America are often Democratic strongholds — a data point that is up sharply since the last protest. "America is at an inflection point," said Randi Weingarten, president of the American Federation of Teachers. "People are afraid, and they can't afford basic necessities. It's time the administration listened and helped them build a better life rather than stoking hate and fear."

title: Thousands fill Quiapo Church for Palm Sunday
content: MANILA — Thousands of Catholic faithful flocked to the Minor Basilica & National Shrine of Jesus Nazareno on Sunday to commemorate Jesus Christ’s triumphant entry into Jerusalem, known as Palm Sunday. The celebration began with a solemn procession from Carriedo Street to the Basilica, where devotees waved their palms for blessing. Palm Sunday signals the start of Holy Week. The day’s Gospel reading focused on the Passion Narrative, recounting the final events in the life of Jesus Christ, including His arrest, trial, suffering, carrying of the cross, and crucifixion. During the reading, priests are joined by lectors who also recite parts of the narrative. "Ating natunghayan na ang sinakyan talaga ng ating Panginoon papunta sa Jerusalem ay hindi pandirigmang kabayo na sumisimbolo ng kapangyarihan at lakas, kundi isang asno o donkey," Licuanan said. "Kagaya ng Panginoong Hesus, tanggapin natin: Mamatay kung mamatay pero hindi ako gagawa ng mga bagay na ikasasama ko sa harap ng Panginoon," he added. Some devotees traveled from provinces to attend the services. Among those who traveled from provinces to attend was Seb Berres from Dasmariñas, Cavite. It is his tradition to visit three churches every year: Quiapo Church, the National Shrine of Our Mother of Perpetual Help in Baclaran, and the National Shrine of Our Lady of Peace and Good Voyage in Antipolo. He brought along his niece, who was attending Quiapo for the first time. "Naisipan kong mag-abroad tapos syempre kailangan ng help… pagkatapos mag-apply, magsisimba sa Quiapo," he said. “Siguro blessing na nakapunta ako sa ibang bansa sa tulong ng [Diyos]. Kaya every year, kailangan ko masimbahan yung tatlong yun.” Friday of Sorrows observed as Catholics honor Mary’s grief ahead of Holy Week Mary Jane Suyat, who traveled from La Union, prayed for a safe trip to Qatar as she prepares to return as an OFW after two decades. She attended the Mass with her nephew and aunt, also first-timers at Quiapo. “Bumyahe po ako [papuntang Quiapo] bago papuntang ibang bansa. Gusto ko sana ma-blessan dito sa Nazareno,” she said. On her first experience at Quiapo Church, she shared: “Magaan sa loob. Pagpasok ko pa lang, e talaga yung pakiramdam ko talaga na-accept niya ako.” According to the church administration, a total of 12 Masses are scheduled today. Morning services are held hourly from 6 a.m. to 11 a.m., while afternoon Masses are at 12:15 p.m., 3 p.m., 4 p.m., and 5 p.m., with evening services at 6 p.m. and 7 p.m. Security personnel at Quiapo Church reported the following attendance figures earlier in the morning: Meanwhile, Church authorities reminded attendees to take care of themselves and their belongings while inside the basilica and advised bringing water due to the hot weather.

title: Iran accuses US of plotting ground attack despite diplomatic talk
content: A view of a damaged residential neighborhood following a military strike on the Iranian capital Tehran on March 15, 2026. Atta Kenare, AFP TEHRAN, Iran -- The speaker of Iran's parliament accused the United States on Sunday of plotting a ground attack despite publicly pushing for a negotiated deal, after a US warship with around 3,500 military personnel arrived in the Middle East. Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf's comments come after more than a month of aerial bombardments by Iran by US and Israeli forces, and as key regional players met to hold talks in Pakistan. The war has escalated into a regional conflagration as Iran has retaliated with attacks on Gulf states, sending energy markets into a tailspin and threatening the world economy. "The enemy publicly sends messages of negotiation and dialogue while secretly planning a ground attack," Ghalibaf said in a statement carried by the official IRNA news agency. "Our men are waiting for the arrival of the American soldiers on the ground to set them on fire and punish their regional allies once and for all," he added. The USS Tripoli, an amphibious assault ship carrying around 3,500 Marines and sailors, arrived in the Middle East on Friday. The Washington Post reported the Pentagon was preparing plans for weeks of ground operations -- potentially including raids on sites near the Strait of Hormuz -- though US President Donald Trump has yet to approve any deployment. 'Strait of Trump': US president says Iran must open key waterway Iran says it has effectively blocked the Strait of Hormuz, a vital shipping lane which previously accounted for a quarter of the world's seaborne oil trade, to hostile shipping. Trump has repeatedly spoken of diplomatic contacts with Iran, although these claims have been denied by Tehran. Pakistan, acting as a go-between for Washington and Tehran, hosted foreign ministers from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Egypt in Islamabad for talks on the crisis. The four-way meeting between the top diplomats of the Muslim nations was slated to discuss "a range of issues, including efforts to de-escalate tensions in the region", Pakistan's foreign ministry has said. - 'All of Tehran was shaking' - In Tehran, two blasts shook the city early Sunday, an AFP journalist said, although it was not clear what was targeted. The Qatari news channel Al Araby said an Israeli missile hit the building housing its office in the city. Footage from inside the office showed broken windows and shattered glass. Outside, images showed the streets covered in debris and damage to surrounding buildings. The channel said in a statement to AFP that it "condemns this attack on a civilian commercial building and affirms that endangering journalists or considering them targets runs counter to international law". "I miss a peaceful night's sleep," an artist in Tehran told AFP, saying night-time strikes were "so intense it felt like all of Tehran was shaking". READ: Iran says US, Israeli strikes damage 120 museums, historic buildings Farzaneh, a 62-year-old woman in Iran's western city of Ahvaz contacted by AFP from Paris, said: "People wake up each day worried about an uncertain future." Ghalibaf on Sunday called for unity among Iranians, saying the country was in "a major global war" that was "at its most critical stage". "We are certain that we can punish the United States, make it regret attacking Iran, and firmly secure our legitimate rights," he said. - Strikes on industry in Gulf - Iranian forces said they had fired a volley of missiles and drones at plants belonging to two of the world's largest aluminium producers in Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates, targeting what they described as industries linked to the US military. Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) said an Iranian attack wounded six and caused significant damage to its plant, while Bahraini state media said two Aluminium Bahrain (ALBA) employees were injured in a second attack. As the specter of a widening conflict grew, Yemen's Houthis on Saturday claimed their first attack of the war, firing what they described as "a barrage of cruise missiles and drones" at strategic sites in Israel. The attacks raised concern about the war spreading to the Red Sea, with Saudi Arabia rerouting much of its oil exports there to avoid Hormuz. During Israel's recent war in Gaza, the Houthis, claiming solidarity with the Palestinians, attacked shipping in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden, forcing companies to take costly detours. On another front, Israeli attacks have continued in Lebanon, which was drawn into the war when Tehran-backed Hezbollah fired rockets at Israel on March 2. On Saturday, the Israeli military killed three journalists in the south. READ: 'No Kings' protests — Trump critics rally across the US Lebanese authorities, including President Joseph Aoun and Prime Minister Nawaf Salam, condemned the killings as war crimes, while Israel alleged that one of the slain reporters was also a member of an elite Hezbollah combat unit. Hundreds of people gathered in the rain for the funeral of the three journalists near Beirut on Sunday. An Israeli strike on an ambulance belonging to the Hezbollah-affiliated Islamic Health Committee killed one paramedic and his patient Sunday, the group's spokesperson said. The incident came a day after at least nine first aid workers were killed by Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon. On Sunday the Israeli army announced the death in combat of a soldier in south Lebanon. At a vocational institute north of Beirut, displaced mother Nasima Ismail signed up her children for services despite few resources as the war interrupts education for hundreds of thousands of students. "I want them to complete their education, even if we are left with nothing," she said. "I wish them days better than ours."

title: Driver sa viral 'gas-and-run' incident may profile na—QCPD
content: Contributed photo/ABS-CBN News/File MAYNILA — May profile na ang Quezon City Police District ng driver ng sasakyan na tumakas matapos magpa-full tank sa isang gasolinahan sa Balintawak, Quezon City. Sa exclusive video na nakuha ng ABS-CBN News, kita ang isang lalaki na bumaba sa puting sasakyan sa may EDSA Caloocan hatinggabi ng March 22. Lumabas na ilang minuto ito bago siya nagpakarga sa target na gasolinahan sa Balintawak. Sa iba pang anggulo ng CCTV, kita na may takip na ang plaka nito sa likuran. Ayon sa pulisya, malaki ang tsansa na sa oras na ito tinakpan ng suspect ang likurang plaka ng kanyang sasakyan. "More or less 5'2 to 5'5 yung height niya, wearing black shirt and pants at naka-slippers. Kitang-kita sa CCTV na lumabas siya at may chineck sa kanyang likuran. Isa pong magandang footage yan, malalaman na natin, ine-enhance na ng cybercrime group itong CCTV para lumiwanag at makita natin ang mukha niya," sabi ni Police Brigadier General Randy Glenn Silvio, Director ng Quezon City Police District. Gas and run? Driver tumakas matapos magpa-full tank sa QC Nakakalat na rin ang mga tauhan ng PNP sa iba't ibang pangunahing kalsada gaya ng mga expressway para suyurin ang mga CCTV. "Tuloy-tuloy po ang pag-iimbestiga natin sa case na ito. Ang mga tropa natin nasa field pa rin, nagre-review po ng forward at backtracking ng footages ng mga CCTV at meron na rin tayong suspect dito. Meron na rin tayong forward projection natin, meron din tayong tropang naka-standby sa NLEX, SLEX may mga numbers ng combination ng plaka na ni-request na tayo," sabi ni Silvio. "Kung ako lang po ang nasa kanyang katayuan, mas maganda nang mag-report siya sa kanyang barangay at magpaliwanag at sumurrender para mas madali na ang pag-iimbestiga, habang tinatagalan niya yung pagtatago niya o hindi siya nagpapakilala," dagdag niya. Nagpaabot na rin ng tulong ang pulisya sa pump attendant matapos malamang ikakaltas sa empleyado ang natangay na P5,196 na halaga ng diesel sa gas station. "Nag-contribute po yung ating mga police officers, from La Loma, para po tumulong sa gasoline boy," sabi ni Silvio. Sa mga may impormasyon sa kinaroroonan o pagkakakilanlan ng driver ng sasakyan, makipag-ugnayan lamang sa pinakamalapit na tanggapan ng PNP. Sakaling maaresto ang suspek ay posible siyang maharap sa reklamong estafa.

title: Comelec en banc impeachment sought
content: The Palacio Del Gobernador headquarters to the Commission on Elections in Intramuros Manila on Nov. 11, 2021. Jonathan Cellona, ABS-CBN News MANILA — A group of lawyers wants the impeachment of the Commission on Elections en banc for alleged betrayal of public trust, other high crimes, and violations of the Republic Act 8436 or the automated election system law. The lawyers, Marvin Aceron and Sikini Labastilla, were joined by Robby Kwan Laurel, who introduced himself as a social entrepreneur, in a press conference at the Club Filipino, Monday morning. The group admitted no congressman has so far endorsed the complaint, which is a constitutional requirement before the House of Representatives can even entertain it. The first is for alleged culpable violation of Republic Act 8436 for deploying software version 3.5.0 in all 110,000 automated counting machines used in the May 12, 2025 elections — which they claimed was not the source code subjected to the mandatory review. The second article alleged betrayal of public trust for installing and operating an unauthorized intermediary server through which all election results were routed before reaching the five accredited transparency servers — leaving Parish Pastoral Council for Responsible Voting (PPCRV) and National Citizens' Movement for Free Elections (Namfel) without results for over two hours after polls closed. WRAP: Alleged issues in automated Halalan 2025 The third article accused Comelec Chairman George Erwin Garcia of betrayal of public trust for concealing the deployment of a single private IP address for 20,300 vote-counting machine modems. "Confident ako kasi ang pinakaunang ebidensya dito are direct admissions of Commissioner Garcia himself. Siya mismo ang umamin sa lahat ng pagkakamali nila. And I'm pretty sure maraming mga taong nadaya dyan dahil sa mga pinagagawa nila," Aceron said. The final charge alleged the respondents committed betrayal of public trust for "the systematic and selective enforcement" of campaign finance laws. "Look at all their credentials. They do not have any outstanding academic record. None of them. What they have are political affiliations," Aceron said of the Comelec en banc. Garcia said the complaint raised "old issues" that he had previously addressed. "Ang resulta at credibilidad  ng 2022 at 2025 eleksyon ay napatunayan ng random manual audit, mga revision ng balota sa iba't ibang posisyon at lugar, mga citizens' arm, observers, at kinilala ng international community," he said.

title: PH in a good location to be a data center hub: DICT
content: MANILA — The Philippines needs to capture what Information and Communications Technology Secretary  Henry Aguda described as the “next oil”— data. At the 3rd Telco Forum organized by the Anti-Red Tape Authority (ARTA), Aguda said the country is positioned to become a data center hub of the region because of the country’s strategic location and ongoing economic reforms. READ: Biz groups working with ARTA to speed up business permit reform He said fiber optics pass through the Philippines linking Asia with the US and other parts of the world, without having to pass through conflict zones like the Middle East. “If you go by the geography of the Philippines, we straddle the Pacific and the ASEAN side of the ocean. We’re in between. There’s no way for them to go through the equator without going through Luzon or Mindanao,” Aguda said. “If there’s Hormuz Strait for oil, there’s the Philippines for the next oil- which is data,” he added, saying this adds opportunities for transit toll revenues. Aguda said the conflict has challenges and opportunities for the country, and one opportunity is in the data center business. “Because of the conflict regions, they are now looking for a new place to locate their data and guess where they’ll locate it in. It’s going to be the Philippines,” he said. They are also reviewing a data sovereignty act and a data embassy policy to entice foreign companies to store their data in the Philippines, which has a growing data center industry. Currently, the Philippines has about 200 MW capacity of data centers. The DICT chief added: “Meta is already crossing the Philippines through the bypass. I won’t name names but two more of the major operators are going to go through the Philippines. Soon, the three household names that provide our social media platforms will go to the Philippines.” Because of this, ARTA wants to further streamline the processes to build data centers in the country. ARTA Secretary Ernest Perez admits there are still challenges, but he hopes agencies can improve the system and implement the reforms. “Always the challenge about the implementation. We’re looking at the LGU level. We’re looking at simplification of permitting process,” Perez said. He added, “We have Executive Order 32, we have Konektadong PInoy, we have the E-Gov Act recently passed, the challenge now is how to implement this.” There are several data centers in the country and more are being built due to the high demand for such facilities especially with rise of artificial intelligence.

title: Suspek sa 'gas and run' sa gasolinahan sa Balintawak, sumuko na sa pulisya
content: MAYNILA — Sumuko na sa La Loma Police Station 1, Lunes ng gabi ang suspek na nag “gas and run” sa isang gasoline station sa Balintawak, Quezon City noong Marso 22. Sinabi ni Police Lt. Col. Jose Luis Aguirre na sa pamamagitan ng back tracking ay natunton ang kinaroroonan ng suspek. “Galing po siya ng Bulacan, nakausap po kasi namin yung may-ari ng sasakyan at kinausap niya ‘tong driver niya na sumuko nalang at para maibigay niya rin yung sagot niya sa mga katanungan natin,” ani Aguirre. Emosyonal naman na nagpaliwanag ang suspek na napag-alamang isang TNVS driver. Depensa niya, halos wala na itong kinikita sa trabaho at ₱100 hanggang ₱150 na lang ang kanyang naiuuwi dahil sa mahal na gasolina bukod pa na matumal na ang biyahe kaya niya nagawang takbuhan ang gasoline station. “Kasi wala po akong mauwing pera. Hindi na po ‘to mauulit,” paliwanag ng suspek. Humingi rin siya ng tawad sa gasoline station staff. “Humihingi po ako ng pasensya sa ginawa ko,” dagdag pa niya. Nag-harap na rin ang biktimang gasoline boy at ang suspek sa police station. “Panatag naman na po ako kasi sumuko naman na po siya,” sabi ng biktima. Pero ayon sa biktima, malaking trauma ang naging epekto sa kanya ng nangyaring pagtakas ng “gas and run” suspek. “Trauma po. Sa bawat karga ko, akala ko kung ano na eh. Kung tatakbuhin po ba. Hindi ako makapag-focus,” aniya. Mahaharap sa reklamong estafa ang nasabing suspek.

title: How to gracefully say no to family and friends selling stuff you don’t need
content: It’s tough when the people you love start acting like a sales agent. And this happens to many of us, and many times more than our wallet can afford. Maybe a cousin launches a side hustle, or a friend starts selling skincare, or you are added by your Mom’s friend to a group chat for her latest “business.” You want to be supportive but you also don’t want to buy things you don’t need.  It can be tricky but if you don’t want to end up with matching pajama sets, another vacuum cleaner, or an AI-powered cookware, you’ll have to learn to say no. Here are 7 ways you can protect your wallet without ruining the relationship. You don’t need a long explanation. The more you say, the higher the chances you’ll end up getting convinced.  Keep it simple with “I’m trying to cut back on spending right now”. Put the blame on your budget, and not the product they are pushing.  Most people will understand but if they don’t, that’s not on you. You can also give a practical excuse, something like you bought something similar recently and have had what you need for quite a while.  This is time-tested for consumable products like kitchen towels, laundry detergents, even milled rice.  Not only will you get a pass this time, but the pass can extend to weeks or months. If you can’t support the product, try to support the salesperson instead.  Do they have a social media page you can share to your followers?  Or maybe a photo with a detailed post you can forward to your group chats?  Even naming referrals who you think might be interested (though I suggest check with your referrals first).  By being helpful, you can preserve the relationship without costing you money. #4 Talk about your decluttering phase One of the rules we try to follow at home is one in, one out.  If we want to buy a new pair of shoes, we check what we have and which one can be donated, sold, or thrown away.  This helps keep our closets, our home and our lives more manageable.  Feel free to copy our rule and use this lifestyle as a shield to push back on buying new things. Some family and friends invite themselves to your home to share their product.  These demos can put a lot of pressure on you, leading to an impulse buy.  To manage their expectations, before they even start, share that you don’t buy anything on the same day.  You have to sleep on it and think if it’s a good fit.  You’ll discover it is easier to say no the next day or the next week. Be honest about your needs.  If you don’t cook, buying cookware does not make sense.  If you don’t wear make-up, whatever you buy will surely go to waste.  If your home is fitted with blinds, no point in switching to curtains.  Remember that every unnecessary purchase adds up and eats into your savings or investments. #7 Tell them to check back later Do this only if there is hope you will consider the purchase.  Because some of the offers can be good.  Like an insurance policy you need.  Or a juice cleanse that will help your health and wellness journey.  So you are saying no for now, but it can be a yes later when you have the cash. In the end what will really help is to say no.  Practice makes perfect so keep saying it and hopefully it will save you next time you feel cornered.

They are also reviewing a data sovereignty act and a data embassy policy to entice foreign companies to store their data in the Philippines, which has a growing data center industry. Currently, the Philippines has about 200 MW capacity of data centers. The DICT chief added: “Meta is already crossing the Philippines through the bypass. I won’t name names but two more of the major operators are going to go through the Philippines. Soon, the three household names that provide our social media platforms will go to the Philippines.” Because of this, ARTA wants to further streamline the processes to build data centers in the country. ARTA Secretary Ernest Perez admits there are still challenges, but he hopes agencies can improve the system and implement the reforms. “Always the challenge about the implementation. We’re looking at the LGU level. We’re looking at simplification of permitting process,” Perez said. He added, “We have Executive Order 32, we have Konektadong PInoy, we have the E-Gov Act recently passed, the challenge now is how to implement this.” There are several data centers in the country and more are being built due to the high demand for such facilities especially with rise of artificial intelligence.

title: Cardinal David presides over Mother Ignacia's cause for beatification relaunch
content: The cause for the beatification and canonization of the Religious of the Virgin Mary (RVM) congregation foundress, Venerable Mother Ignacia del Espiritu Santo, was relaunched on Wednesday, according to a CBCP News report. Mother Ignacia, the report stated, is the foundress of the first pontifical congregation for women in the Philippines. And in recognition of her heroic virtues, was declared venerable in 2007. Kalookan Bishop Cardinal Pablo Virgilio David, who presided over the Mass that marked the relaunch said "visible signs of grace" is the parameter in which to measure the progress in the cause for canonization. “This is also what we now await in the cause of the venerable Mother Ignacia—not so much new documents, but a clear and credible sign of God’s action through her intercession,” David said during the Mass held at the RVM Generalate Chapel in Quezon City. “You are not only remembering a text. You are celebrating a fiat — a yes that continues to live on in your community and ministry,” he added. The theological consultant for the Ignacian Mission for Sainthood, RVM Sr. Maria Anicia Co, told Radio Veritas that the relaunch was conducted because "previously submitted miracle claims failed to meet the standards of a medical review panel." “We relaunched because the submitted miracles did not really pass the medical panel’s evaluation… by 2016, there seems to be a lull,” Co said. According to the CBCP News report, Co said the process was slow because of a lack of reports of miraculous healings that are needed for the cause. In order to address this, the congregation has decided to "strengthen documentation and coordination efforts." The RVM also appointed vice postulators, including Dr. Dave Cesar Dela Cruz for external affairs and Sr. Eloisa Marie Inocentes for internal affairs and other members of the Ignacian Mission for Sainthood. “It’s not only Mother Ignacia for sainthood, but each one of us to become truly saints,” she said. Cardinal David also administered the oath to the members of the team. — BAP, GMA Integrated News

title: LIST: Tips to safeguard your home during a Holy Week vacation
content: As several Filipinos are set to travel for the Holy Week break, authorities are reminding the public not to overlook home safety. Leaving a house unattended, even for a few days, can increase the risk of theft, fire, and other accidents. A report from Unang Balita highlighted practical steps households can take to keep their homes secure while away: Before leaving, make sure all doors, windows, and gates are properly locked. Double-checking entry points is one of the simplest yet most effective ways to prevent break-ins. Homeowners are also advised to avoid leaving spare keys in obvious places such as under doormats or plant pots. Unplugging electrical appliances and switching off the main power supply can help prevent fire incidents. This is especially important for devices that may overheat when left unattended. For households using liquefied petroleum gas, regulators should be turned off before leaving to avoid leaks that could lead to explosions or fires. Posting travel plans in real time on social media can alert potential intruders that a house is empty. Authorities advise sharing vacation updates only after returning home. Keeping a low profile about travel schedules adds an extra layer of security. If possible, inform a trusted neighbor, friend, or relative about your trip. They can periodically check the house, collect mail, or monitor any unusual activity. Some homeowners also install lights on timers to make it appear that someone is inside. Important items such as gadgets, cash, and documents should be kept in secure places before leaving. Locking cabinets or using safes can reduce the risk of loss in case of break-ins. Taking a few precautionary steps before going on vacation can significantly reduce risks at home. While travel offers a chance to relax, ensuring that your house is safe allows for greater peace of mind while you are away. —Sherylin Untalan/ VAL, GMA Integrated News

title: IOC's gender policy divides opinion as supporters and critics clash
content: LONDON - Reactions to the International Olympic Committee's new policy on gender testing were sharply divided on Thursday, with supporters hailing a long-overdue move to protect women's sport and critics warning it risks stigma and harm to young athletes. Supporters of the decision said it was essential for the governing body to reassert the importance of a protected female category and to provide clarity for sports organizations worldwide. Fiona McAnena, Director of Campaigns for UK-based advocacy group Sex Matters, called the ruling "extremely welcome". "Women's sport can only be for those who are female," McAnena told Reuters in an interview. "The IOC sets the standard for sport worldwide. It's very welcome that the IOC has recognized that the only way to have fair sport for women and girls is to have a protected female category." She said it was crucial for the IOC to take the lead, rather than leaving individual sports to navigate the issue alone. "Their influence is enormous," she said. "Many sports used the IOC's previous policies to justify not protecting the female category. That's why I'm really pleased the IOC has called this policy 'protecting the female category'." McAnena rejected the idea that broader inclusion automatically increases participation. "We know that women and girls drop out of sport when they are forced to compete with boys, or when they find that changing rooms or playing fields are not single sex when they thought they would be," she said. While broadly supportive, McAnena said there were elements of the policy that fell short. She criticised the IOC's decision not to backdate the rules, saying it failed to address past injustices. "We know that three women were cheated of medals in the Rio Olympics, deprived let's say, by male athletes with disorders of sex development in the 800 meters," she said. "It seems a shame that that cannot be put right for those three women." At the 2016 Games, Caster Semenya, Francine Niyonsaba and Margaret Wambui claimed the medals in the women's 800 metres, with all three classified as having differences of sexual development (DSD). All three have been ineligible to compete in the women’s 800 meters since 2019, after World Athletics introduced tightened eligibility regulations covering events from 400 meters to one mile. The rules require athletes with DSD to medically reduce naturally high testosterone levels in order to compete in those events. Semenya refused to do so, arguing the regulations were discriminatory and violated her rights. Wambui has not competed since the rules were implemented seven years ago, while Niyonsaba switched to longer distances. McAnena also pointed to an exception in the policy for athletes with the diagnosis of Complete Androgen Insensitivity Syndrome (CAIS), saying it still allowed for some male advantage, even if reduced. Opponents of the IOC's ruling, however, argue it is not backed by solid science and risks harm to athletes, particularly girls and minors. Dr. Payoshni Mitra, founder of advocacy group Humans of Sport, described the ruling as "a safeguarding disaster" and said it appeared to be driven more by politics than by science. "It's not science-based, it's stigma-based," Mitra said in an interview with Reuters. "It's more under political pressure rather than really what is required in women's sport." Mitra said she was "shocked" that the policy includes minor athletes, since it will encompass all athletes competing in female category events at the Olympics, Youth Olympics and Games qualifiers. "As far as I know, there were about 14 minor athletes competing in the Paris Olympics," Mitra said. The youngest of those was 11-year-old Chinese skateboarder Zheng Haohao. She also questioned the timing of the decision, suggesting political considerations around the next Summer Olympics in Los Angeles played a role. "(The U.S.) is a country where we are very aware that things are going in a direction which is not what progressive-minded people expected," she said. "The IOC could have focused on robust, independent research. But they rushed into this decision, which tells me this is all because of where the Summer Olympics is going to be hosted next." Mitra said sex-based eligibility rules have historically had a disproportionate impact on women from Africa and Asia. Double Olympic gold medallist Semenya was one of nine African women athletes with alleged sex variations who wrote to IOC president Kirsty Coventry on Wednesday. A similar letter had previously been sent to the President by Semenya in June 2025. "When I was asked to be consulted, I made one thing clear: I will not be used as a token voice," Semenya said. "Consultation means nothing if you have already decided. It means nothing if you have not sat with our stories, our pain, what our bodies have been put through in the name of sport. "If the IOC had truly listened — if President Coventry had done what evidence-based policy demands — this policy would not exist. It does not smell of science. It smells of stigma. It was not born from care for athletes. It was born from political pressure. "As a woman from Africa, I had hoped President Coventry would be different. I had hoped she would listen to all of us — not just the powerful, not just the comfortable. She failed us." World Athletics in 2023 banned transgender women who had gone through male puberty from competing and tightened its DSD rules, lowering permitted testosterone thresholds and making eligibility contingent on sustained medical suppression. Women competing at last year's world championships had to have a one-off gene test to comply with requirements. "We have led the way in protecting women’s sport over the last decade," a World Athletics spokesperson said on Thursday. "Attracting and retaining more girls and women into sport requires a fair and level playing field where there is no biological glass ceiling. This means that gender cannot trump biology. A consistent approach across all sport has to be a good thing."

title: Pasig court orders ocular inspections of KOJC properties
content: A Pasig court on Friday ordered ocular inspections of Kingdom of Jesus Christ (KOJC) properties in Davao, Quezon City, and Pasig City to gain a clearer understanding of the premises identified in the qualified trafficking case against the religious group's founder, Apollo Quiboloy, and other co-accused. In a 9-page order dated March 27, the Pasig Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch 159 granted the motion of the prosecution and ordered ocular inspections of the following: The RTC stated that during her cross-examination, the complainant sketched the relevant areas within the KOJC compound. It said that while the sketch aids the RTC in understanding the layout and relative locations, it remains limited to the complainant's recollection. "Here, the Court finds it necessary to conduct an ocular inspection of the following subject premises, as such inspection will materially assist the Court in obtaining a clearer and more accurate understanding of the locations where the alleged offenses… were purportedly committed, and of the manner in which these properties were allegedly utilized as instruments in the commission of the offenses," it said. According to the court, the ocular inspections of the properties located in Pasig and Quezon City will be on April 27 while the inspection on properties in Davao will be on May 18. "The prosecution and counsels for all the accused are likewise directed to be present during the conduct of the ocular inspection," it said. This came after the prosecution asked the RTC to conduct an ocular inspection, arguing that this will allow the court to better appreciate the evidence presented in Quiboloy’s qualified trafficking case on sexual exploitation and labor trafficking. The RTC stressed that the inspection is authorized only to help the court in clearing a doubt, reaching a conclusion, or finding the truth. "But it is not the main trial nor should it exclude the presentation of other evidence which the parties may deem necessary to establish their case," it said. GMA News Online has asked Quiboloy's camp for comment. Quiboloy is also facing charges under Section 5(b) and  Section 10(a) of Republic Act 7610 or the Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation, and Discrimination Act. — VDV, GMA Integrated News

title: Commuters at PITX experience longer waits as buses decrease due to oil costs
content: The impact of successive mega oil price hikes is now being felt at the Parañaque Integrated Terminal Exchange (PITX), prompting some bus operators to reduce the number of units in operation.Long lines of passengers can be seen at PITX. Unlike before, when buses arrived continuously, commuters say trips are now more limited and arrive only intermittently.“Ngayon ko lang po naranasan na matagal po mag-antay ngayon na hindi rush hour po. Antay lang po kasi wala na po ibang sasakyan.” Christine, an affected passenger said. (This is the first time I experienced waiting for a long period outside of the rush hour. But I have no choice because there's no other vehicle available.)Bus drivers and personnel from a bus line confirmed that they have indeed reduced the number of operating units.“Mga 80. Dati? Opo, ngayon mga 50 na lang siguro yung tumatakbo. Ang taas po kasi ng krudo, sobrang taas kaya malulugi po yung kumpanya,” bus driver Josephine Guevarra said. (From 80, we now only have 50 plying the routes. Oil prices are too steep, plying would just result in losses for the company.)“Dati mam, ano mam, 9 to 10 units po. Ngayon, ma’am, parang lima na lang siya. Apat. Kasi siyempre ma’am, yung kita, ma’am, hindi na po kagaya ng dati. Talagang ang laki po nang binaba nung sales po namin.” Jobelle Tamang, a bus line staff said. (We used to have 9 to 10 units, now we have 5 or 4.  Sales really dipped.)According to PITX, the situation poses a major challenge, especially with the expected increase in passengers during Holy Week.“The main challenge now would be the supply. Kasi ilan sa mga operators natin nagpahayag na talaga na dahil sa taas ng presyo ng gasolina, nagbabawas na sila ng mga biyahe nila. Tulad ng sa Batangas City, sa San Jose, Nueva Ecija, sa Pangasinan, no? And in fact, iba sa kanila nagbabalak pa magbawas kasi nga nahihirapan na sila.” Jason Salvador, head of PITX Corporate Affairs and Government Relations, said. (Several operators have said that they would reduce their bus units because of the high oil price, such as in Batangas City, San Jose, Nueva Ecija, Pangasinan.)Passenger volume is also increasing, as more commuters opt for public transportation due to high fuel costs.“Napakataas ng gasolina, pansin natin na mas tumataas pa yung bilang ng mga pasahero dahil, one, yung iba sa kanila na dating nagdadala ng sariling sasakyan ay… nagpa-public transport na lang.” Salvador said. (We observe an increase in the number of commuters as some motorists are now taking public transport due to the expensive gas.)Despite this, PITX assured the public that buses will still be available, though waiting times are expected.“Yes, oo. Ma-assure naman natin yun. Yun nga lang, magkakaroon ng waiting time. Mas gusto nila, ide-deploy lang nila yan kung fully booked na. So, meaning, ang epekto nito, maghihintay. Maghihintay yung mga pasero kasi unless puno na, hindi sila mag-provide ng units at hindi rin i-deploy.” Salvador added. (Buses will be available, but commuters have to bear the longer wait because buses will be deployed only once they are fully booked.)Some passengers are choosing to travel earlier than usual to avoid congestion and possible fare increases.“Nagbiyahe na para hindi masyadong congested. At, yun nga, baka yung fear na baka umakyat yung pamasahe. At least nauna na nang konti… para magkita kita naman kahit minsan lang sa isang taon. May effort talaga kasi hindi naman madali magbyahe,” Generoso Comia who is traveling with family said. (We travelled early because fares might go up. We really want to take this trip to visit our relatives, whom we don't often see.)Others, like Rachel Cabigao, traveled to Manila with her family to spend Holy Week with her husband, a tricycle driver.“Kailangan mamasada siya direcho para kahit papano hindi siya lugi. Ang laki po kasi nang tinaas ng gas eh… pinaglalaanan po talaga namin ng pera tsaka oras para makabyahe. Pamilya bonding… para makalakihan din ng mga bata. Makita din nila yung tradisyon namin every Semana Santa. Kaya yun, niluluwas din namin yung mga bata," Rachel Cabigao, who traveled from Cavite, said. (He needs to continuously be on the road to earn. We saved money to travel to Manila and see him to have family bonding. It's a tradition during Holy Week.)Meanwhile, some passengers are still willing to travel despite fare increases.“70 plus pesos ang itinaas… Siyempre mahalaga po yun. Yung makasama mo yung mahal sa buhay ng kahit saglit lang iba yung pakiramdam. Tapos, makikita mo yung mga kamag-anak mo nagsisi-uwian. Parang family reunion na rin,” Perlita Almodovar, who is traveling to Nueva Ecija, said. (There was P70 increase in fare.  But we need to be with our loved ones, like a family reunion.)Strict security measures remain in place at PITX, including X-ray machines and K9 units.In recent days, authorities have confiscated numerous prohibited items such as bladed objects, scissors, lighters, and aerosol cans.PITX also advised passengers to immediately report any illegal fare overcharging.For those planning to travel this Holy Week, authorities strongly recommend booking tickets in advance to avoid long waiting times, especially as some operators may further reduce their bus units.—LDF, GMA Integrated News

title: EXPLAINER: How the new Malampaya gas well will benefit Filipinos
content: Malacañang on Friday explained the significance of drilling and testing the Camago-3 well, an indigenous energy source in offshore Palawan, as the country faces fuel supply concerns amid the Middle East conflict. Citing information from the Presidential Communications Office, Sandra Aguinaldo reported on "24 Oras" that the Camago-3 well can produce up to 60 million standard cubic feet of gas each day, enough to power around one million households. On Thursday, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. made the announcement regarding the Camago-3 well. Marcos said the Camago-3 holds an estimated 2.5 times more recoverable gas than the Malampaya East-1 discovery. “Together, these two wells are projected to extend the life of the Malampaya gas field by an estimated six years,” he said. Marcos added that the latest discovery means a steadier and cheaper power supply for the country. “Malampaya gas costs us roughly P4.80 per kilowatt-hour. Imported LNG costs P10.30. More than double,” Marcos said. “Every unit of power we generate from Malampaya instead of imported fuel is money saved by households, by small businesses, by every Filipino who pays an electricity bill,” he added. Following the successful drilling, completion, and flow test in Camago-3, Prime Energy, the gas division of business magnate Enrique Razon's Prime Infrastructure Capital Inc., stated that it is on track to start producing natural gas from the Malampaya Phase 4 (MP4) by late 2026. "The next major step is the drilling of the Bagong Pag-asa exploration well, located about 30 kilometers north of Malampaya. If gas is confirmed, the well will undergo drill-stem testing to assess its production potential,” Prime Energy said in a statement. Prime Energy leads the Malampaya Consortium, with joint venture partners UC38 LLC., Prime Oil & Gas Inc., and PNOC Exploration Corp. —Jiselle Anne Casucian/VBL, GMA Integrated News
